title: The Enrolment Lock-In: Why Private Schools Commit to Next Year's Payroll Before Next Year's Fees Are Confirmed
linkedin:
A private school makes its biggest financial commitment of the year in spring, and it isn't enrolment day.

It's the moment next year's staffing establishment gets locked in.

Teaching positions are confirmed or advertised through August and September, built against a projected enrolment number rather than a confirmed one. A class needs a teacher whether it holds twenty two students or twenty six, so most of that cost is fixed the moment the establishment is set.

The fee revenue that pays for it won't be fully known for months. Some families confirm early, some wait until Term 4, some are quietly weighing a move without saying so.

There's a second gap hiding underneath the first one. A steady enrolment number doesn't guarantee steady fee revenue. Sibling discounts, bursaries and early-payment concessions sit between the published fee schedule and what actually lands, so average net fee per student can quietly fall even while headcount holds flat.

The schools that manage this well don't try to forecast enrolment more precisely. They build the year backward from what's already committed, staffing and fixed costs as the known side, realistic fee timing as the variable side, laid out term by term rather than compared only at the annual level.

That's the difference between finding a tight week before you're in it, and finding out after.
